title: The first filled knot is the first crossing
claim: W1: a knot-local move attaches a cone over the graph of its old pairs, so the knot complex's b2 never falls and b1 grows by (components - 1) less the rank of that graph's loops in K. W2: a filled knot (four distinctions carrying four knots, each the middle of one) forces two crossing splits in any presentation without copies. W3: along KF3, NN, NN2 and SEEDK from a bracketing, no crossing, no filled knot, b2 = 0 and no fill yet are equivalent at every step. W4: b2 depends on the presentation (saturated lines), the filled-knot reading does not in its forcing direction.
